name: security

findings.message: The `matches` op uses `[[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]]` with no validation that `$expected` is a well-formed ERE: an invalid regex causes bash to return exit code 2, the `&&` short-circuits, `_match` stays "false" and no error is emitted — the predicate silently never matches, reproducing the exact silent-fail-open mode (safety abort never fires) the issue was designed to eliminate; the numeric ops have an explicit guard for invalid operands but `matches` has none.
Same unvalidated-regex silent-fail issue in the `_cycle_check_until` single-condition path: `matches)  [[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]]` with no ERE well-formedness check.

Same unvalidated-regex silent-fail issue in `_cycle_check_abort_when`: `matches)  [[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]]` with no ERE well-formedness check; for abort_when specifically, a silently-invalid regex means the safety abort switch never fires.

All three evaluators accept `ne|neq` instead of `neq` only: the design decision stated "rename `ne` to `neq`" in the evaluators, but the change added `neq` as an alias while retaining `ne`, so `ne` never reaches the `*) error` branch (SPEC-8's defense-in-depth) and silently evaluates; SPEC-3 requires `ne` to be refused, but runtime enforcement is bypassed for any path (test fixture, direct variable injection, pre-fix state) that bypasses the template loader.
`ne|neq` alias kept in `_cycle_check_until` single-condition evaluator, same SPEC-8 bypass as line 478.

`ne|neq` alias kept in `_cycle_check_abort_when` evaluator, same SPEC-8 bypass as line 478; because abort_when is the safety switch, a `ne`-op predicate that reaches runtime silently evaluates rather than refusing, undermining defense-in-depth on the most critical predicate.

In `_tpl_validate_cycles`, `until.op` validation is guarded by `if [[ -n "$uo" ]]; then`, so a template whose `until:` block omits the `op:` key entirely passes template load without error (caught only at runtime by `_cycle_load_template`); the SPEC guarantees "refused at template load" but the guard silently narrows that to non-empty ops only.

reason: the security lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
